To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Keck Cosmic-Web Imager (KCWi) provides the first kinematic evidence for multi-filament accretion onto galaxies at high redshifts, and the first evidence for the inflows that build galaxies at the peak epoch of star formation.
we have developed a suite of models for the first time that can kinematically isolate the inflow of cold gas from the cosmic filamentary web onto a young galaxy at the peak of cosmic star formation.

the Multi-Filament inflow model provides a robust description of cold mode accretions onto young star forming galaxies, and is a powerful new technique for studying the kinematics of the circum-galactic medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinematics and dynamics of gas in galaxies at the peak epoch of star formation, and how it is accreted from the cosmic web.
the kinematic signatures of cold-mode accretion in the early Universe, as seen in the Ly{\alpha} emission from the intergalactic medium.
the kinematic properties of the gas in galaxies at the peak epoch of star formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the KCWI data and the multi-filament inflow models presented here provide evidence that cold accretion from filaments is a viable mode of gas delivery to the centers of high-redshift galaxies.
we have identified the cold mode of accretion in two Ly{\alpha}-emitting galaxies around high-redshift QSOs.
the inflows are sufficient to fuel the galaxies and are consistent with cold flow accretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a method for detecting cold mode accretions in high-redshift galaxies.
we have shown the existence of multi-filament inflows, which are a key component of cold accretion.
the KCWI data is a strong indication of cold mode accretions, which is a major component in the growth of the galaxy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the KCWI can be used to directly observe the accretion of cosmic web material onto young star-forming galaxies.
KCWI's high spatial resolution is crucial to detecting the cold-mode accretion that fuels star formation.
we have demonstrated a new technique for mapping the gas flows in the cosmic web.
